questions.question: In September 2023, which Chief Minister of an Indian state won the Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship for his distinguished contribution to public service?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himanta Biswa Sarma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Himanta Biswa Sarma is the Chief Minister of Assam, a state in northeastern India.
 
• He was awarded the Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship in September 2023.
 
• This fellowship is given in recognition of his distinguished contribution to public service.
 
• The Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship aims to foster international understanding and collaboration by bringing outstanding leaders to Singapore.
 
• Himanta Biswa Sarma has been instrumental in implementing various developmental initiatives in Assam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship**

 
 
• Named after Singapore's founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew.
 
• It is awarded to outstanding individuals who have contributed significantly to their respective fields and countries.
 
• The fellowship promotes the exchange of ideas and experiences between Singapore and other countries.
 
• Fellows are invited to Singapore to gain insights into its development experience.
 
 
 
• **Himanta Biswa Sarma's Contributions**
 
 
• He played a key role in improving healthcare and education infrastructure in Assam.
 
• Under his leadership, Assam has seen significant economic development and social reforms.
 
• He has been a prominent figure in the Indian political landscape, with a focus on regional development.
 
 
 
• **Assam State**
 
 
• Located in northeastern India, known for its rich culture and biodiversity.
 
• It is famous for its tea plantations and Assam silk.
 
• Assam has a diverse population with various ethnic groups and languages.

questions.question: Gulbarga and Bidar style of architecture was patronised by which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahmani dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bahmani dynasty was a Muslim state of the Deccan in South India and one of the great medieval Indian kingdoms.
 
• Gulbarga and Bidar were the capital cities of the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• The Bahmani rulers patronized Persian culture and learning, which significantly influenced the architectural styles in the region.
 
• Notable architectural contributions include the Jama Masjid of Gulbarga and the Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan in Bidar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bahmani Sultanate:**

 
 
• Founded by Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah in 1347.
 
• It was the first independent Muslim kingdom in South India.
 
• It split into five successor states known as the Deccan Sultanates by the end of the 15th century.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• Blend of Persian, Turkish, and local architectural styles.
 
• Extensive use of arches, domes, and minarets.
 
• Elaborate tile work and stucco decorations.
 
 
 
• **Gulbarga:**
 
 
• Known for its fort and the grand Jama Masjid.
 
• The mosque features a unique design with a large dome and numerous smaller domes.
 
 
 
• **Bidar:**
 
 
• Famous for the Bidar Fort and the Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan.
 
• The Madrasa is an Islamic seminary with a grand architectural design.

questions.question: Which food is a good source of complete protein?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eggs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Eggs are one of the most complete sources of protein available, containing all nine essential amino acids.
 
• They are highly digestible and have a high biological value, meaning the body can utilize the protein efficiently.
 
• Each large egg contains approximately 6 grams of high-quality protein.
 
• Eggs are not only protein-rich but also packed with essential vitamins and minerals, including vitamin B12, vitamin D, and selenium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Complete Proteins:**

 
 
• Complete proteins contain all nine essential amino acids that the body cannot produce on its own.
 
• Besides eggs, other complete protein sources include meat, fish, dairy products, and quinoa.
 
 
 
• **Biological Value (BV):**
 
 
• BV is a measure of how efficiently the body can use a protein.
 
• Eggs have a BV of 100, making them a benchmark for comparing other protein sources.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits of Eggs:**
 
 
• Eggs can help with muscle maintenance and repair due to their high protein content.
 
• They are also beneficial for eye health, thanks to antioxidants like lutein and zeaxanthin.
 
 
 
• **Amino Acids:**
 
 
• Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.
 
• Essential amino acids must be obtained from the diet, as the body cannot produce them.

questions.question: The property of rock or soil that indicates the ability of allowing fluids to flow through it is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Permeability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Permeability** is a measure of the ability of a material (such as rock or soil) to transmit fluids.
 
• It is an important property in **hydrogeology**, **soil science**, and **petroleum engineering**.
 
• Permeability is influenced by the size, shape, and connectivity of the pores in the material.
 
• Materials with high permeability, like sand and gravel, allow fluids to flow through them easily.
 
• It is typically measured in units of area, such as **Darcy (D)** or **millidarcy (mD)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Porosity:**

 
 
• Porosity refers to the volume of pores or voids in a material and is expressed as a percentage of the total volume.
 
• High porosity does not necessarily mean high permeability; it depends on the connectivity of the pores.
 
 
 
• **Hydraulic Conductivity:**
 
 
• It is a specific measure of permeability that quantifies the ease with which water can move through pore spaces or fractures.
 
• Hydraulic conductivity is typically measured in meters per second (m/s).
 
 
 
• **Capillary Action:**
 
 
• This is the ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of external forces, often against gravity.
 
• It is a critical factor in soil moisture movement and plant water uptake.
 
 
 
• **Darcy's Law:**
 
 
• A fundamental equation that describes the flow of a fluid through a porous medium.
 
• It states that the flow rate is proportional to the pressure drop and the permeability of the material.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT associated with the ‘Prarthana Sabha’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was a reform movement founded in 1867 in Bombay to make social and religious reforms in the Hindu society.
 
• Govind Ranade, RG Bhandarkar, and Atmaram Pandurang were prominent leaders associated with the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• The Samaj aimed at removing caste restrictions, encouraging widow remarriage, and promoting women's education.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi, although a prominent figure in Indian history, was not associated with the Prarthana Samaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Govind Ranade**

 
 
• Govind Ranade was a distinguished Indian scholar and social reformer.
 
• He played a significant role in the formation of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Ranade was also a judge of the Bombay High Court and an advocate for social reforms such as widow remarriage and the abolition of child marriage.
 
 
 
• **RG Bhandarkar**
 
 
• Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indian scholar, social reformer, and a prominent member of the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He made significant contributions to the fields of Sanskrit and ancient Indian history.
 
• Bhandarkar was also involved in the establishment of the Bombay Anthropological Society.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang**
 
 
• Atmaram Pandurang was the founder of the Prarthana Samaj.
 
• He was a physician and social reformer who worked towards the upliftment of the downtrodden sections of society.
 
• His efforts were directed towards promoting rational and progressive thinking in the Hindu community.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He is known for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and his role in leading India to independence from British rule.
 
• Gandhi was associated with various movements like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: Air and National Defence are examples of which of the following goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Public goods** are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, meaning they can be used by everyone without preventing anyone else from using them.
 
• Examples of public goods include **air** and **national defense**, as they are available to all citizens without restrictions.
 
• The provision of public goods is typically the responsibility of the government due to their nature of being non-excludable.
 
• Public goods are funded by the government through taxation as they are essential for societal well-being and economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common goods**

 
 
• These are goods that are non-excludable but rivalrous, meaning their use by one person can reduce availability for others.
 
• Examples include fish stocks in the ocean and public pastures.
 
 
 
• **Club goods**
 
 
• These are goods that are excludable but non-rivalrous, meaning they can be restricted to paying customers but one person’s use does not reduce availability for others.
 
• Examples include subscription-based services like cable TV.
 
 
 
• **Private goods**
 
 
• These are goods that are both excludable and rivalrous, meaning they can be owned and consumed by individuals, and their use by one person prevents use by another.
 
• Examples include food, clothing, and cars.
 
 
 
• **Free-rider problem**
 
 
• This occurs when individuals can benefit from a good without paying for it, which is common with public goods.
 
• It can lead to under-provision of these goods if not managed by the government.

questions.question: Captain Hawkins visited India during the reign of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Captain William Hawkins arrived at the court of the Mughal Emperor Jahangir in 1609.
 
• Hawkins was sent by the English East India Company to establish trade relations with the Mughal Empire.
 
• He brought a letter from King James I of England to Jahangir, seeking permission to trade in India.
 
• Jahangir granted Hawkins a favorable reception and allowed the English to establish a factory at Surat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jahangir's Reign**

 
 
• Jahangir, also known as Salim, was the fourth Mughal Emperor of India, ruling from 1605 to 1627.
 
• He was known for his administration, art patronage, and the establishment of many gardens across the empire.
 
• His reign was marked by relative stability and expansion of the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **English East India Company**
 
 
• Founded in 1600, the English East India Company was a British trading company that established trade routes and settlements in India.
 
• It played a crucial role in the British colonization of India.
 
• Its primary goal was to trade in spices, cotton, silk, indigo, and other goods.
 
 
 
• **Mughal-English Relations**
 
 
• The visit of Captain Hawkins marked the beginning of formal relations between the Mughal Empire and England.
 
• Subsequent visits by other English envoys led to the establishment of more factories and trading posts in India.
 
• These relations eventually paved the way for British colonial rule over India.
 
 
 
• **Surat Factory**
 
 
• The factory at Surat was the first English factory established in India in 1612.
 
• It became an important trading post for the English East India Company.
 
• Surat's port was strategic for trade with Persia, the Arabian Peninsula, and Europe.

questions.question: Which type of molecules show dipole-dipole interaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Molecules possessing permanent dipole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dipole-dipole interactions occur between molecules that have permanent dipoles.
 
• The positive end of one polar molecule attracts the negative end of another polar molecule.
 
• These interactions are stronger than London dispersion forces but weaker than hydrogen bonds.
 
• Examples of molecules showing dipole-dipole interactions include hydrogen chloride (HCl) and sulfur dioxide (SO2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transient Dipole:**

 
 
• Transient dipoles are temporary dipoles that arise due to the momentary distribution of electrons within a molecule.
 
• They are responsible for London dispersion forces, which are present in all molecules but are the only type of intermolecular force in non-polar molecules.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Molecules:**
 
 
• Ionic molecules consist of positively and negatively charged ions.
 
• The intermolecular forces between ionic molecules are known as ionic bonds, which are significantly stronger than dipole-dipole interactions.
 
 
 
• **Non-Polar Molecules:**
 
 
• Non-polar molecules have no permanent dipole moment.
 
• The primary intermolecular forces in non-polar molecules are London dispersion forces.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonds:**
 
 
• Hydrogen bonds are a special type of dipole-dipole interaction.
 
• They occur when hydrogen is directly bonded to highly electronegative elements like fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.
 
• Hydrogen bonds are stronger than regular dipole-dipole interactions due to the high polarity of the involved bonds.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded by Shiv Prasad Gupta and Bhagwan Das in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1921**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded in the year **1921**.
 
• The institution was established by **Shiv Prasad Gupta** and **Bhagwan Das**.
 
• It is located in **Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The university was initially known as **Kashi Vidyapith** and was later renamed to honor Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The university was set up as a response to the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**

 
 
• It was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement from British rule.
 
• It was led by Mahatma Gandhi after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British occupation in India through nonviolent means.
 
 
 
• **Shiv Prasad Gupta**
 
 
• A prominent Indian philanthropist and freedom fighter.
 
• He played a crucial role in the establishment of various educational institutions in India.
 
 
 
• **Bhagwan Das**
 
 
• An Indian theosophist, scholar, and freedom fighter.
 
• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1955, India's highest civilian award.
 
 
 
• **Varanasi**
 
 
• Also known as Benares or Kashi, it is one of the oldest living cities in the world.
 
• It is a major cultural and religious hub in India, particularly for Hindus.

questions.question: From which of the following countries was the concept of the Fundamental Duties borrowed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the **Constitution of Russia (formerly USSR)**.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976 during the Emergency period in India.
 
• Initially, there were **ten Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• An additional duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002, making the total number of Fundamental Duties eleven.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act**

 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its comprehensive scope.
 
• Enacted in 1976 during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• Introduced significant changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists Fundamental Duties for every citizen.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens about their moral obligations to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to support the unity of India.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, these duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act**
 
 
• Enacted in 2002, this amendment made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Article 21A was introduced, and the Right to Education became a constitutional guarantee.
 
• An additional Fundamental Duty was introduced for parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children.

questions.question: Darshana Jhaveri, a famous Manipuri dancer, was awarded the Padma Shri in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Darshana Jhaveri is a renowned Manipuri dancer who has made significant contributions to the field of Manipuri dance.
 
• She was awarded the prestigious Padma Shri in the year 2002 for her contributions to the arts.
 
• The Padma Shri is India's fourth highest civilian award, recognizing distinguished service in various fields.
 
• Darshana Jhaveri, along with her sisters, is part of the Jhaveri Sisters, a group known for popularizing Manipuri dance.
 
• Her dedication to preserving and promoting Manipuri dance has earned her national and international acclaim.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri Dance**

 
 
• Manipuri dance is one of the major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, often performed to the accompaniment of traditional Manipuri music.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the region's culture and often depicts scenes from the life of Krishna.
 
• Manipuri dance incorporates both Hindu Vaishnavism themes and elements of the region's ancient folklore and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award**
 
 
• The Padma Shri is India's fourth highest civilian award, established in 1954 by the Government of India.
 
• It recognizes distinguished contributions in various fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award consists of a medal and a certificate signed by the President of India.
 
• Padma Shri awardees are announced annually on the occasion of Republic Day.
 
 
 
• **Jhaveri Sisters**
 
 
• The Jhaveri Sisters are a renowned group of Manipuri dancers, comprising Nayana, Ranjana, Suverna, and Darshana Jhaveri.
 
• They have played a significant role in popularizing Manipuri dance both in India and abroad.
 
• The sisters have been honored with numerous awards for their contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• Their performances often highlight the rich cultural heritage and intricate storytelling of Manipuri dance.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dances of India**
 
 
• India is home to several classical dance forms, each with its unique style, history, and cultural significance.
 
• Some of the major classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• These dance forms are often characterized by their elaborate costumes, intricate footwork, and expressive gestures.
 
• Classical dances are an important part of India's cultural heritage, often performed at festivals, celebrations, and cultural events.

questions.question: For how many days is the Chhat Puja celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhat Puja is a significant Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Usha (Chhathi Maiya).
 
• It is celebrated over a period of four days, with each day having its own unique rituals and significance.
 
• The festival is most prominently observed in the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and the country of Nepal.
 
• The four days of Chhat Puja include Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya, and Usha Arghya.
 
• Devotees observe rigorous fasting, holy bathing, and offer prayers to the setting and rising sun during the festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nahay Khay:**

 
 
• The first day of Chhat Puja, where devotees take a holy dip in a river or water body and prepare the traditional meal.
 
• It signifies the beginning of the purification process both physically and spiritually.
 
 
 
• **Kharna:**
 
 
• The second day involves a day-long fast that ends in the evening after performing rituals and offering kheer (a rice pudding) to the deity.
 
• Devotees abstain from drinking water during this fast until the evening rituals are completed.
 
 
 
• **Sandhya Arghya:**
 
 
• The third day, devotees offer arghya (offerings) to the setting sun, followed by a night-long vigil.
 
• This day is marked by the preparation of various traditional delicacies and the gathering of the community for the evening rituals.
 
 
 
• **Usha Arghya:**
 
 
• The fourth and final day involves offering arghya to the rising sun, marking the end of the fasting period.
 
• Devotees break their fast after the morning rituals and share prasad (sacred food) with the community.

questions.question: The Maukharis ruled over _______ in western Uttar Pradesh, which later on replaced Pataliputra as the political centre of northern India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanauj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maukharis initially ruled over the region around **Kanauj**, which is situated in western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Kanauj later became a significant political center in northern India, replacing Pataliputra.
 
• The Maukharis were contemporaries and sometimes adversaries of the later Gupta rulers.
 
• Kanauj's strategic location made it a focal point of power struggles among various northern Indian dynasties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maukharis Dynasty**

 
 
• The Maukharis were an important dynasty that ruled parts of northern India, especially in the region of present-day Uttar Pradesh.
 
• They are known from inscriptions and coins that have been discovered in the area.
 
• The dynasty reached its peak under King Ishanavarman, who successfully resisted the later Guptas and expanded his territory.
 
• The Maukharis eventually declined and their territories were absorbed by the later Harsha Empire.
 
 
 
• **Kanauj**
 
 
• Kanauj is an ancient city in Uttar Pradesh, India, known historically for its strategic importance.
 
• It served as the capital of several dynasties, including the Maukharis, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and later the Gahadavalas.
 
• Kanauj was a major center of trade and culture during its time as a political center.
 
• The city is also mentioned in classical Indian literature and historical texts.
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra**
 
 
• Pataliputra, now known as Patna, was the ancient capital of the Magadha kingdom.
 
• It served as the political and cultural center of various Indian empires, including the Maurya and Gupta Empires.
 
• The city was known for its impressive architecture and was one of the largest cities in the world during ancient times.
 
• Pataliputra's decline began after the fall of the Gupta Empire, with other cities like Kanauj rising in prominence.

questions.question: Kishori Amonkar, one of the finest classical singers of Hindustani music, was from which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kishori Amonkar** was a renowned classical singer of Hindustani music.
 
• She was born on **10 April 1932** in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• Kishori Amonkar was a prominent figure in the **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana** tradition of Indian classical music.
 
• She was known for her **innovative and emotional interpretations** of classical compositions.
 
• Amonkar received several prestigious awards, including the **Padma Bhushan (1987)** and **Padma Vibhushan (2002)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**

 
 
• One of the two main forms of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It originated in North India and is known for its complex ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Prominent gharanas (musical schools) include Jaipur-Atrauli, Gwalior, and Kirana.
 
 
 
• **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**
 
 
• Founded by Alladiya Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• Known for its intricate and elaborate raga structures.
 
• Emphasizes on the purity of notes and complex taans (rapid melodic sequences).
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• One of the highest civilian honors in India.
 
• Conferred in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• Awards are given for distinguished service in various fields such as arts, science, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **Classical Music Awards**
 
 
• Various organizations and governments confer awards to recognize excellence in classical music.
 
• Some notable awards include the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Tansen Award.

questions.question:
Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II.

List I:

(a) Endoplasmic reticulum

(b) Vacuoles

(c) Golgi apparatus

(d) Mitochondria

List II:

(i) for packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them to various targets.

(ii) generates ATP.

(iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents.

(iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Endoplasmic reticulum (a) - (iv)**: It serves as channels for the transport of proteins.
 
• **Vacuoles (b) - (iii)**: These are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents.
 
• **Golgi apparatus (c) - (i)**: It is involved in the packaging of materials synthesized near the ER and dispatching them to various targets.
 
• **Mitochondria (d) - (ii)**: It generates ATP, which is the energy currency of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**

 
 
• It is a network of membranous tubules within the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell.
 
• There are two types: Rough ER (with ribosomes) and Smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**
 
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles found in both plant and animal cells.
 
• In plant cells, a large central vacuole maintains turgor pressure, which is crucial for maintaining the plant's structural integrity.
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are smaller and often involved in storage and transport.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• Also known as the Golgi complex or Golgi body.
 
• It is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or for use within the cell.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**
 
 
• Known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell’s supply of ATP.
 
• They are double-membraned organelles with their own DNA, which suggests they were once independent prokaryotic organisms.
 
• Mitochondria are involved in other processes like signaling, cellular differentiation, and the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Blossom Shower, also known as Pre-monsoon showers, is primarily associated with the state of Kerala and parts of Karnataka, not Andhra Pradesh.
 
• These showers occur in the months of March and April, marking the transition period before the onset of the southwest monsoon.
 
• This phenomenon is crucial for the growth of crops such as coffee and spices in Kerala and Karnataka.
 
• The showers help in the blossoming of coffee flowers, which is why they are also referred to as 'Coffee Showers'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nor'westers**

 
 
• Known locally as 'Kalbaisakhi', these are violent thunderstorms occurring in West Bengal and parts of Bangladesh during the pre-monsoon months of April and May.
 
• They are characterized by strong winds, heavy rain, and sometimes hail.
 
• These storms are vital for the cultivation of jute and rice in the region.
 
 
 
• **Bordoichila**
 
 
• Bordoichila is a local thunderstorm occurring in Assam during the pre-monsoon season, typically in late April to early May.
 
• These storms are named after the mythical Assamese bride 'Bordoichila' who is believed to visit her mother’s home during this time.
 
• They bring heavy rain and strong winds, which are important for tea cultivation in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Mango Showers**
 
 
• Mango showers are pre-monsoon showers that occur in parts of South India, including Kerala and Karnataka.
 
• These rains are crucial for the ripening of mangoes, hence the name 'Mango Showers'.
 
• They usually occur from March to May and provide relief from the summer heat.

questions.question: In which state is the Jhumming cultivation known as Dahiya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jhumming cultivation is a traditional form of shifting agriculture practiced in various states of India.
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, this form of agriculture is specifically known as Dahiya.
 
• It involves clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning vegetation, then cultivating crops on it for a few years before moving to a new area.
 
• Dahiya is practiced mainly by the tribal communities in the hilly regions of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This method is part of the cultural heritage and agricultural practices of these tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation**

 
 
• It is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned and allowed to revert to their natural vegetation.
 
• This cycle is repeated as the farmer moves to a new area.
 
• Shifting cultivation is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture.
 
• It is commonly practiced in tropical rainforests and hilly terrains.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Shifting cultivation can lead to deforestation and loss of biodiversity if not managed sustainably.
 
• It can also cause soil erosion and degradation over time.
 
• Sustainable practices are necessary to mitigate these environmental impacts.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Communities**
 
 
• Tribal communities in India often rely on traditional agricultural practices like shifting cultivation.
 
• These practices are deeply rooted in their cultural and social systems.
 
• Government policies and programs aim to support sustainable agricultural practices among tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Policies**
 
 
• The Indian government has various schemes to promote sustainable agriculture and support farmers.
 
• Programs focus on improving agricultural productivity, sustainability, and farmers' livelihoods.
 
• Efforts include providing training, financial assistance, and access to modern agricultural technologies.

questions.question: 'Gaur Maria' dance is performed in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gaur Maria Dance** is a traditional dance form performed by the **Maria tribe** of Chhattisgarh.
 
• This dance is predominantly observed in the **Bastar district** of Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is performed during **festivals and important community events** such as weddings and harvest celebrations.
 
• The dance involves vibrant costumes, traditional instruments like the **mandar** (drum), and rhythmic movements that depict the **daily activities and rituals** of the Maria tribe.
 
• Gaur Maria dance is recognized for its **energetic performance** and is an integral part of the **cultural heritage** of Chhattisgarh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bastar District**

 
 
• Bastar is one of the key districts in Chhattisgarh known for its rich **tribal culture** and traditions.
 
• This region is home to several indigenous tribes, including the Marias, Murias, and Halbas.
 
• Bastar hosts the famous **Bastar Dussehra**, a unique and long-standing festival that lasts for 75 days.
 
• The district is also renowned for its **handicrafts and traditional artwork**.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Culture in Chhattisgarh**
 
 
• Chhattisgarh has a significant tribal population, with tribes such as the Gond, Muriya, Maria, Bhatra, and Halba contributing to the state's cultural mosaic.
 
• These tribes have their own distinct **customs, dialects, and traditional practices**.
 
• Traditional dances, music, and handicrafts play a vital role in the socio-cultural life of these tribes.
 
• Tribal festivals often feature elaborate rituals and are an expression of their close relationship with nature.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Instruments**
 
 
• The Maria tribe uses several traditional musical instruments during their dance performances, including the **mandar**, **tudbudi** (a type of drum), and **jhumki** (ankle bells).
 
• These instruments are essential in creating the rhythmic beats that accompany the dance movements.
 
 
 
• **Costumes in Gaur Maria Dance**
 
 
• The performers wear vibrant and elaborate costumes featuring **feathers, beads, and traditional jewelry**.
 
• Men typically wear headgear adorned with **peacock feathers** and other decorative elements.
 
• Women wear colorful sarees and accessorize with intricate jewelry, enhancing the visual appeal of the dance.

questions.question: The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was hosted by _______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was held in **England** in 2009.
 
• This tournament marked the inception of the Women's T20 World Cup, organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• England emerged as the champions of the inaugural tournament by defeating New Zealand in the final.
 
• The final match of the tournament was played at the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground in London.
 
• The tournament featured a total of 8 teams participating from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Women's T20 World Cup**

 
 
• It is a biennial international championship for women's Twenty20 International cricket.
 
• The tournament is organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• It aims to promote women's cricket and increase its popularity globally.
 
• Australia has been the most successful team in the tournament's history with multiple titles.
 
• The tournament provides a platform for showcasing talent and increasing the visibility of women's cricket.

• **International Cricket Council (ICC)**
 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket.
 
• It was founded as the Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 and later renamed the International Cricket Council in 1989.
 
• The ICC is responsible for organizing major international cricket tournaments, including the Cricket World Cup and T20 World Cup.
 
• It sets the rules and regulations for the sport and promotes the growth of cricket worldwide.
 
• The ICC has over 100 member countries, including full members, associate members, and affiliate members.

questions.question: Who among the following became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships event?

__
 
• Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships.
 
• He achieved this milestone in the men's javelin throw event.
 
• Neeraj's winning throw was recorded at 88.17 meters.
 
• He had previously won gold at the Tokyo Olympics 2020, marking his historic achievement in athletics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Athletics Championships**

 
 
• It is a biennial athletics event organized by World Athletics (formerly IAAF).
 
• The event features various track and field competitions, attracting top athletes from around the globe.
 
• The first World Athletics Championships were held in Helsinki, Finland, in 1983.
 
 
 
• **Javelin Throw**
 
 
• Javelin throw is a track and field event where the competitor throws a spear-like implement, called a javelin, as far as possible.
 
• The technique involves a run-up, followed by a throw from behind a designated line.
 
• The javelin must land tip first within a specified sector to be considered a valid throw.
 
 
 
• **Neeraj Chopra's Achievements**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra won gold at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, becoming India's first track and field athlete to win an Olympic gold medal.
 
• He is also a Commonwealth Games gold medallist, having won in 2018.
 
• Chopra has been awarded several honors, including the Arjuna Award and the Khel Ratna Award, for his contributions to Indian sports.

• Neeraj Chopra's gold medal at the World Athletics Championships is a historic achievement for Indian athletics.
 
• It highlights the growing potential and talent in India's track and field athletes on the global stage.
 
• His achievements have inspired a new generation of athletes in India to pursue excellence in sports.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution mentions that, "There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court such salaries as may be determined by the Parliament by law, and until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries are specified in the Second Schedule"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 125**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 125 of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the salaries of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• It stipulates that the salaries of the Judges shall be determined by the Parliament by law.
 
• Until such a provision is made by the Parliament, the salaries are specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures that the financial independence of the judiciary is maintained, which is crucial for upholding the principle of judicial independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 124**

 
 
• Deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Specifies the process of appointment of the Chief Justice and other Judges of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Article 126**
 
 
• Provides for the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice of India.
 
• An Acting Chief Justice is appointed when the office of the Chief Justice is vacant or when the Chief Justice is unable to perform the duties of the office.
 
 
 
• **Article 127**
 
 
• Deals with the appointment of ad hoc Judges in the Supreme Court.
 
• Allows the Chief Justice of India to request retired Judges to sit and act as a Judge of the Supreme Court for a temporary period.
 
 
 
• **Second Schedule of the Constitution**
 
 
• Specifies the emoluments, allowances, and privileges for various constitutional offices including the President, Governors, Judges, etc.
 
• Ensures a structured and transparent approach towards the remuneration of key public officials.

questions.question: Who is the writer of the novel 'A Suitable Boy'?

• **Vikram Seth** is the author of the novel **'A Suitable Boy'**, which was published in 1993.
 
• The novel is one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume in the English language, consisting of 1349 pages.
 
• 'A Suitable Boy' explores the story of a young girl, Lata, and her quest to find a suitable husband, set in the post-independence, post-partition era of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following initiatives of the Government of India promises 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to all the rural households who volunteer to do unskilled manual work?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) was enacted in September 2005.
 
• The scheme aims to enhance the livelihood security of people in rural areas by guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to a rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• MGNREGS covers all districts of India except for those that have a 100% urban population.
 
• The scheme is demand-driven, meaning work is provided when it is demanded by the rural households.
 
• It aims to create durable assets and strengthen the livelihood resource base of the rural poor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Funding Pattern**

 
 
• The cost of wages for unskilled manual workers is shared between the Central and State Governments in a 90:10 ratio.
 
• The central government bears the full cost of wages for semi-skilled and skilled workers and material costs.
 
 
 
• **Implementation**
 
 
• MGNREGS is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) in association with state governments.
 
• The Gram Panchayats are the principal authorities for planning and implementation of the scheme at the grassroots level.
 
 
 
• **Social Audit**
 
 
• Social audits are conducted by the Gram Sabha to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation of the scheme.
 
• Social audits involve a public process where the work done by the Gram Panchayat is scrutinized by the community.
 
 
 
• **Impact**
 
 
• MGNREGS has significantly contributed to poverty alleviation, especially among marginalized communities.
 
• The scheme has also been instrumental in creating rural infrastructure and improving access to basic amenities.

questions.question: Who among the following personalities said, "What I object to is the ‘craze’ for machinery as such. The craze is for what they call labour-saving machinery. Men go on ‘saving labour’ till thousands are without work and thrown to the open streets to die of starvation."?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement known for his philosophy of nonviolence and civil disobedience.
 
• He criticized the over-reliance on machinery and industrialization, emphasizing the importance of manual labor and self-reliance.
 
• The quote reflects Gandhi's concern about the adverse effects of industrialization on employment and the livelihood of workers.
 
• Gandhi advocated for the empowerment of rural India through the promotion of cottage industries and traditional crafts.
 
• His views on machinery and labor are part of his broader philosophy of "Swaraj" (self-rule) and "Sarvodaya" (welfare of all).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swaraj:**

 
 
• Swaraj means "self-rule" and was a key concept in Gandhi's philosophy, emphasizing political independence and self-governance.
 
• It also includes economic independence through self-sustained communities and local self-government.
 
 
 
• **Sarvodaya:**
 
 
• Sarvodaya translates to "welfare of all" and signifies Gandhi's vision of a society where the well-being of every individual is considered.
 
• It promotes social justice, equity, and the upliftment of the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Khadi Movement:**
 
 
• Gandhi promoted the use of Khadi (hand-spun and hand-woven cloth) as a symbol of self-reliance and resistance to British industrial goods.
 
• The movement aimed to revive traditional industries and provide employment to rural populations.
 
 
 
• **Critique of Industrialization:**
 
 
• Gandhi believed that excessive industrialization leads to economic disparity, unemployment, and environmental degradation.
 
• He supported the idea of small-scale industries and sustainable practices.
